subject: occuFP example script (occupancy with false positives)

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: occuFP example script (occupancy with false positives)
parts:
hi all,
 the example code in the help file for occuFP has been deficient for a long time so I spent some time this week writing an example script that shows how to simulate and package up data and how to fit different models.  I will clean this up during the summer and make it part of the help file for occuFP for the next release (not until January probably). But for now, here is the script which shows, in succession, how to simulate and fit a model for:

 1. a mix of ordinary occupancy data (no false positives) and some data contaminated with false positives

 2. data which are all contaminated with false positives

 3. occupancy data with no false positives + some contaminated with false positives + some "known true positive" data

 For more detail on what this all means see the help file for occuFP (thanks to David Miller from years ago) as well as read his paper Miller et al. (2011) cited in the help file.

regards,
andy



 
# Read the help file
# Here we simulate some data and we fit a model of type 2 which has some ordinary occupancy data NOT
# subject to false positives and also some that are subject to false positives... we assume a total of
# K=7 sample intervals of which the first 2 are assumed to be subject to no false positives.
# We simulate a habitat covariate and we suppose p varies between the first 2 samples and the last
# 5 which we code with a dummy variable for inputting to the scrFrame
# Sites, reps, and K1 = number of ordinary occupancy reps
M = 200
K = 7
K1= 2
# occupancy model
habitat<- rnorm(M)
alpha0<- 0
alpha1<- 1
psi<- plogis( alpha0 + alpha1*habitat)
z<- rbinom(M, 1, psi)
# Detection parameters and data simulation
y = matrix(0,M,K)
p = c(0.7, 0.5)  # method 2 will have a lower p
fp = 0.05
for(i in 1:M){
# Normal occupancy data
 y[i,1:2]<- rbinom(1, 1, p[1]*z[i])
# False-positives mixed in
 y[i,3:7]<- rbinom(5, 1, p[2]*z[i] + fp*(1-z[i]) )
}
 
## type is a vector with the number of each data type 1, 2, 3 (see help file). In this case, 2 sites are of type 1
## (ordinary occupancy) and 5 sites are of type 2 (contaminated with false positives) and there are no type 3 sites
## These are assumed to be in the corresponding columns of the encounter data matrix. i.e., rows 1-2 are type 1, etc..
type<- c(2, 5, 0)
# one site covariate which is binary (2 groups of sites) and 1 obs covariate which is binary "method"
occ <- matrix(c(rep(0,M*(K-K1)),rep(1,M*K1)),M,K)
siteCovs <- data.frame(habitat = habitat)
obsCovs <- list(METH = occ)
library(unmarked)
umf1 <- unmarkedFrameOccuFP(y,siteCovs = siteCovs, obsCovs = obsCovs, type = type)
m1 <- occuFP(detformula = ~ METH, FPformula = ~1,
             stateformula = ~ habitat, data = umf1)
m1

# Standard unmarked summary functions work with the occuFP models:
head(predict(m1, type = 'fp') )
coef(m1)
confint(m1, type = 'det')

#
# Next we consider a situation where we don't have any perfect occupancy data, only data subject to
# false positives (type 2 data), but the first 2 occasions have a different p from the last 5
# Its important to use starting values for the false positive parameter in this model to
# avoid finding the wrong maximum of the likelihood (see below)
#
M = 200
K = 7
K1= 2  
habitat<- rnorm(M)
alpha0<- 0
alpha1<- 1
psi<- plogis( alpha0 + alpha1*habitat)
z<- rbinom(M, 1, psi)
y = matrix(0,M,K)
p = c(0.7, 0.5)  # method 2 will have a lower p
fp = 0.05
# simulate the data. Note here both chunks of data are simulated with the false positives
for(i in 1:M){
# Normal occupancy data
 y[i,1:2]<- rbinom(2, 1, p[1]*z[i] + fp*(1-z[i]) )
# False-positives mixed in
 y[i,3:7]<- rbinom(5, 1, p[2]*z[i] + fp*(1-z[i]) )
}
 
# type indicates all 7 occasions correspond to false positives data
type<- c(0, 7, 0)
 
# one site covariate which is binary (2 groups of sites) and 1 obs covariate which is binary "method"
occ <- matrix(c(rep(0,M*(K-K1)),rep(1,M*K1)),M,K)
siteCovs <- data.frame(habitat = habitat)
obsCovs <- list(METH = occ)
umf1 <- unmarkedFrameOccuFP(y,siteCovs = siteCovs, obsCovs = obsCovs, type = type)
# starting values are important here or else MLE finds the wrong mode!
m2 <- occuFP(detformula = ~ METH,       FPformula = ~1,
             stateformula = ~ habitat,  data = umf1, starts=c(0,0,0,0, -1) )
m2

#
# now here we will consider some type 3 observations which we will assume exist as column 7 of the
# encounter history data. Remember these take on values 0 not detected, 1 = detected but uncertain, 2 = confirmed occupied
#

M = 200
K = 7
K1= 2  
habitat<- rnorm(M)
alpha0<- 0
alpha1<- 1
psi<- plogis( alpha0 + alpha1*habitat)
z<- rbinom(M, 1, psi)
y = matrix(0,M,K)
p = c(0.7, 0.5)  # method 2 will have a lower p
b<- 0.5  # probability that a false positive is determined to be certain
fp = 0.05
# simulate the data.
for(i in 1:M){
# Normal occupancy data
 y[i,1:2]<- rbinom(2, 1, p[1]*z[i]   )
# False-positives mixed in
 y[i,3:6]<- rbinom(4, 1, p[2]*z[i] + fp*(1-z[i]) )
 # Type 3 observations are occupancy data contaminated with false positives but then we identify some of them as true
 y[i, 7]<- rbinom(1, 1, p[2]*z[i] + fp*(1-z[i]) )
}
  true.positives<- z==1 & y[,7]==1
  confirmed<- (rbinom(M, 1, b) ==1)   & true.positives
  y[confirmed, 7]<- 2
 
# type indicates all 7 occasions correspond to false positives data
type<- c(2, 4, 1)
 
# One site covariate which is binary (2 groups of sites) and 1 obs covariate which is binary "method"
occ <- matrix(c(rep(0,M*(K-K1)),rep(1,M*K1)),M,K)
siteCovs <- data.frame(habitat = habitat)
obsCovs <- list(METH = occ)
umf1 <- unmarkedFrameOccuFP(y,siteCovs = siteCovs, obsCovs = obsCovs, type = type)
# starting values are important here or else MLE finds the wrong mode!  Note: last parameter in this model is "Pcertain"
m3 <- occuFP(detformula = ~ METH,       FPformula = ~1,  Bformula = ~1,
             stateformula = ~ habitat,  data = umf1, starts=c(0,0,0,0, -1, 0) )
m3
# Potentially the parameter b might also depend on covariates, so we accommodate that here.
 
m3b <- occuFP(detformula = ~ METH,       FPformula = ~1,  Bformula = ~ habitat,
             stateformula = ~ habitat,  data = umf1, starts=c(0,0,0,0, -1, 0,0) )
m3b
